words.def: one sign of the alphabet, like A or B
all the letters from A to Z
to say the letters of a word in order
words.ex: How do you spell your name?

words.def: a big letter, like A, not a
words.ex: Names start with a capital letter.

sentences.en: How do you spell your name?
It's O-M-A-R.
Can you repeat that, please?
sentences.ar: هل يمكنك أن تكرّر ذلك من فضلك؟

grammar.title: Spelling and capital letters
grammar.body: We spell words letter by letter. For two letters that are the same, we often say “double”: Hanna = H-A-double N-A. Use a capital letter for names, cities, countries, days and the word I.

examples.en: My name is Hanna: H-A-double N-A.

dialogue.en: Hello! What's your name?
My name is Omar.
How do you spell that?
O-M-A-R. And my email is omar at mail dot com.

words.def: how much money you pay for something
words.ex: What's the price of this bag?

words.def: a question about price or amount
it costs a lot of money

sentences.en: How much is this bag?
It's forty-five dollars.
That's too expensive!

grammar.title: How much…? and -teen / -ty
grammar.body: Ask “How much is…?” for one thing and “How much are…?” for two or more. Listen carefully: thirTEEN (13) has the stress at the end, THIRty (30) has the stress at the start.

dialogue.en: Excuse me, how much is this bag?
It's fifty dollars.
Fifteen or fifty?
Fifty. Five, zero.

sentences.en: What time is it?
It's half past ten.
The class starts at nine o'clock.
sentences.ar: يبدأ الدرس في الساعة التاسعة تمامًا.

grammar.title: Telling the time
grammar.body: Ask “What time is it?” Answer with “It's…”. Use “past” for minutes after the hour and “to” for minutes before the next hour. Use “at” with a time: at 5 o'clock.

examples.en: The bus comes at quarter to eight.
examples.ar: تأتي الحافلة في الثامنة إلا ربعًا.

dialogue.en: Excuse me, what time is it?
It's quarter to nine.
Oh no, my class is at nine!
Hurry! Don't be late.

words.ex: What do you do at the weekend?
There are twelve months in a year.

words.def: the day you were born, every year

words.ex: Today is the first of June.

words.def: the day and month, like 5th May

sentences.en: When is your birthday?
It's on the third of April.
We have class on Monday and Wednesday.

grammar.title: at, on, in for time
grammar.body: Use “at” with clock times (at 6 o'clock), “on” with days and dates (on Friday, on 3rd April) and “in” with months, years and seasons (in May, in 2026, in winter).

examples.en: The party is on Friday at eight.

dialogue.en: When is your birthday, Yusuf?
It's on the twelfth of March. And you?
dialogue.ar: إنه في الثاني عشر من مارس. وأنتِ؟

dialogue.en: Mine is in October, on the first.
dialogue.ar: عيد ميلادي في أكتوبر، في اليوم الأول.

dialogue.en: Great! Let's have a party.

sentences.en: What does your sister look like?
She is tall and she has short hair.
He has green eyes and a beard.

grammar.title: is / has for describing people
grammar.body: Use “is” + adjective for size and age: He is tall. She is young. Use “has” for things on the body: She has long hair. He has a beard. Adjectives come before the noun: long hair, not hair long.

dialogue.en: Who is your new teacher?
Mr Adam. He is tall and young.
Does he have a beard?
Yes, and he has blue eyes.

words.ex: My mother is in the kitchen.

words.def: the room where the family sits
words.ex: We watch TV in the living room.

words.def: glass in the wall, for light
a home on one floor of a building
words.ex: I live in a small flat.

sentences.en: There is a big kitchen in my flat.
There are two bedrooms.
Is there a garden? No, there isn't.
sentences.ar: هل توجد حديقة؟ لا، لا توجد.

grammar.title: There is / There are
grammar.body: Use “There is” for one thing and “There are” for two or more. Questions: Is there…? Are there…? Short answers: Yes, there is. / No, there aren't.

examples.en: There is a sofa in the living room.
Are there any windows? Yes, there are.

dialogue.en: Do you live in a house?
No, I live in a flat. There are three bedrooms.
dialogue.ar: لا، أسكن في شقة. توجد ثلاث غرف نوم.

dialogue.en: Is there a balcony?
Yes, there is. It has a nice view.

words.def: to leave your bed in the morning
to eat the first meal of the day

words.ex: My father goes to work by bus.

words.def: to go and sleep at night
words.ex: I go to bed at eleven.

sentences.en: I get up at seven every day.
My sister goes to school by car.
What time does he come home?

grammar.title: Present simple: he / she / it + -s
grammar.body: We use the present simple for routines. With he, she and it, add -s to the verb: I work → she works. Some verbs add -es: go → goes, watch → watches. have → has. Questions use does: Does she work? What time does he get up?

examples.en: Does she have breakfast? Yes, she does.

dialogue.en: What time do you get up, Omar?
At half past six. Then I have breakfast.
dialogue.ar: في السادسة والنصف. ثم أتناول الفطور.

dialogue.en: And your brother?
He gets up at ten. He doesn't work on Sunday!
dialogue.ar: يستيقظ في العاشرة. هو لا يعمل يوم الأحد!

words.def: a game with a ball and two teams
to look at programmes on TV
words.ex: We watch TV in the evening.

words.def: time when you are not working
words.ex: What do you do in your free time?

sentences.en: What do you do in your free time?
I like swimming and reading.
She doesn't like football.

grammar.title: like / love / don't like + -ing
grammar.body: After like, love and hate we often use a verb + -ing: I like reading. She loves cooking. Negative: I don't like… / He doesn't like… Spelling: swim → swimming, ride → riding.

dialogue.en: What do you do in your free time?
I love playing football. And you?
I don't like football. I like reading.
dialogue.ar: لا أحب كرة القدم. أحب القراءة.

dialogue.en: Me too! I read in bed every night.
dialogue.ar: وأنا أيضًا! أقرأ في السرير كل ليلة.

words.ex: It's very windy by the sea.

sentences.en: What's the weather like today?
It's hot and sunny.
It never snows in my city.

grammar.title: How often? always, usually, sometimes, never
grammar.body: Frequency words show how often: always (100%), usually, often, sometimes, never (0%). They go before the main verb but after “be”: I usually walk. It is always hot.

examples.en: It is always cold in January.

dialogue.en: What's the weather like in your city?
It's usually hot and sunny.
Does it rain?
Sometimes, in winter. It never snows.
dialogue.ar: أحيانًا، في الشتاء. ولا تثلج أبدًا.

words.def: clothes for the top of your body, with buttons
one piece of clothing for women
you wear them on your feet
how big or small clothes are
to put clothes on in a shop to check them
words.ex: Can I try on this jacket?

sentences.en: Can I try on these shoes?
This jacket is too small.
Do you have it in a bigger size?

grammar.title: this / that / these / those
grammar.body: Use “this” (one) and “these” (two or more) for things near you. Use “that” (one) and “those” (two or more) for things far from you.

dialogue.en: Excuse me, can I try on that dress?
dialogue.ar: عفوًا، هل يمكنني تجربة ذلك الفستان؟

dialogue.en: Of course. What size are you?
Medium, please. And these shoes in 38?
dialogue.ar: متوسط من فضلك. وهذا الحذاء مقاس 38؟

dialogue.en: Here you are. The changing room is there.

words.ex: Go straight on for two minutes.

words.def: very near, at the side of
words.ex: The café is next to the bank.

words.def: on the other side of the street
words.ex: The park is opposite the school.

words.def: where you wait for the bus
words.ex: The bus stop is near my house.

sentences.en: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
Go straight on and turn left.
It's opposite the hospital.

grammar.title: Giving directions
grammar.body: We give directions with the base verb (no “you”): Go, Turn, Take. To make it negative, use Don't: Don't turn right. Places: next to, opposite, between, near, on the corner.

examples.en: Take the second street on the right.
The bank is between the café and the shop.

dialogue.en: Excuse me, is there a pharmacy near here?
dialogue.ar: عفوًا، هل توجد صيدلية قريبة من هنا؟

dialogue.en: Yes. Go straight on and turn right.
dialogue.ar: نعم. امشِ مباشرة ثم انعطف يمينًا.

dialogue.en: Is it far?
No, it's next to the bus stop.

words.def: the list of food in a restaurant
words.ex: Can I see the menu, please?

words.def: a person who brings food to tables
to ask for food in a restaurant

words.ex: I'd like ice cream for dessert.

words.def: the paper that shows how much to pay
words.ex: Can we have the bill, please?

sentences.en: I'd like the chicken, please.
Would you like something to drink?
Can we have the bill, please?
sentences.ar: هل يمكننا الحصول على الفاتورة من فضلك؟

grammar.title: I'd like… / Would you like…?
grammar.body: “I'd like” (= I would like) is a polite way to say “I want”. Use “Would you like…?” to offer something. Answers: Yes, please. / No, thank you.

examples.en: I'd like a glass of water.
Would you like some tea? Yes, please.
examples.ar: هل تريد بعض الشاي؟ نعم من فضلك.

dialogue.en: Good evening. Are you ready to order?
dialogue.ar: مساء الخير. هل أنتم مستعدون للطلب؟

dialogue.en: Yes. I'd like the fish and a salad, please.
dialogue.ar: نعم. أريد السمك وسلطة من فضلك.

dialogue.en: Would you like something to drink?
Orange juice, please.

words.def: to move in water using your arms and legs
to sit on a bicycle and move
to make music with a guitar
to say words in a language

sentences.en: Can you drive? Yes, I can.
I can't play the guitar.
She can speak English very well.

grammar.title: can / can't
grammar.body: Use can + base verb for ability. It is the same for all people: I can, he can, they can (never “he cans”). Negative: can't. Question: Can you…? Short answers: Yes, I can. / No, I can't.

examples.en: Can they swim? No, they can't.
examples.ar: هل يستطيعون السباحة؟ لا، لا يستطيعون.

dialogue.en: Can you ride a bike, Lina?
dialogue.ar: هل تستطيعين ركوب الدراجة يا لينا؟

dialogue.en: Yes, I can. Can you?
No, I can't. But I can swim very well.
dialogue.ar: لا، لا أستطيع. لكني أسبح جيدًا جدًا.

dialogue.en: Great! Let's go swimming on Saturday.

words.def: when your body is very hot because you are ill
a noise from your throat when you are ill
something you take to get better
words.ex: Take this medicine twice a day.

sentences.en: What's the matter?
I have a headache and a fever.
You should drink a lot of water.
sentences.ar: يجب أن تشرب الكثير من الماء.

grammar.title: should / shouldn't for advice
grammar.body: Use should + base verb to give advice, and shouldn't for things that are a bad idea. It is the same for all people: you should, he should.

examples.en: You shouldn't go to work today.
examples.ar: لا ينبغي أن تذهب إلى العمل اليوم.

dialogue.en: Hello, Yusuf. What's the matter?
I have a sore throat and a cough.
Take this medicine and drink warm water.
dialogue.ar: خذ هذا الدواء واشرب ماءً دافئًا.

dialogue.en: Should I stay at home?
dialogue.ar: هل يجب أن أبقى في المنزل؟

dialogue.en: Yes, you should rest for two days.

words.ex: I'm going to call you tomorrow.
We're going to travel next week.

words.def: to go and see a person or a place
words.ex: I'm going to visit my aunt.

words.def: days when you don't work or study
words.ex: Where are you going on holiday?

words.def: a paper you buy to travel or see a show
words.ex: I have two tickets for the film.

words.def: something you decide to do later
words.ex: What are your plans for the weekend?

sentences.en: What are you going to do this weekend?
sentences.ar: ماذا ستفعل في عطلة نهاية الأسبوع؟

sentences.en: I'm going to visit my grandparents.
We aren't going to stay at home.

grammar.title: going to for plans
grammar.body: Use am / is / are + going to + base verb for plans you have already decided. Negative: I'm not going to… Questions: Are you going to…? What are you going to do?

examples.en: She is going to buy a new phone.
Are they going to come? Yes, they are.

dialogue.en: What are you going to do this weekend?
dialogue.ar: ماذا ستفعل في عطلة نهاية الأسبوع؟

dialogue.en: I'm going to visit the museum. And you?
I'm going to cook for my family.
Nice! Are you going to make a cake?
Yes, a chocolate cake!

words.def: the evening or night before today

words.ex: I was in Dubai two years ago.

words.def: with a lot of things to do
words.ex: I was very busy at work.

words.def: you need to rest or sleep
words.ex: We were tired after the trip.

sentences.en: Where were you yesterday?
I was at work. I was very busy.
sentences.ar: كنت في العمل. كنت مشغولًا جدًا.

sentences.en: Were you tired? Yes, I was.

grammar.title: was / were
grammar.body: “was” and “were” are the past of am / is / are. I / he / she / it → was. you / we / they → were. Negative: wasn't, weren't. Questions: Was he…? Were you…?

dialogue.en: Where were you last night? You weren't at the party.
dialogue.ar: أين كنت الليلة الماضية؟ لم تكن في الحفلة.

dialogue.en: I was at home. I was very tired.
dialogue.ar: كنت في المنزل. كنت متعبًا جدًا.

dialogue.en: Oh! Was it a busy day?
Yes, it was. Was the party good?
It was great!

words.ex: I watched a film last night.
I stayed at home on Sunday.

sentences.en: What did you do last weekend?
sentences.ar: ماذا فعلت في عطلة نهاية الأسبوع الماضية؟

sentences.en: I cleaned the house and watched TV.
Did you study? No, I didn't.

grammar.title: Past simple: regular verbs
grammar.body: For finished actions in the past, add -ed: play → played, watch → watched. Spelling: study → studied, stop → stopped. Negative and questions use did + base verb: I didn't play. Did you play?

dialogue.en: Did you have a nice weekend, Sara?
dialogue.ar: هل قضيتِ عطلة جميلة يا سارة؟

dialogue.en: Yes! I visited my cousins. We played games.
dialogue.ar: نعم! زرت أبناء عمي. لعبنا ألعابًا.

dialogue.en: Did you watch the match on Saturday?
No, I didn't. I studied for the test!

words.ex: My friends came to my house.

sentences.en: Last Friday we went to the sea.
sentences.ar: يوم الجمعة الماضي ذهبنا إلى البحر.

sentences.en: We ate lunch and saw the sunset.
Did you buy anything? Yes, I bought a hat.
sentences.ar: هل اشتريت شيئًا؟ نعم، اشتريت قبعة.

grammar.title: Past simple: irregular verbs
grammar.body: Many common verbs do not add -ed. Learn them: go → went, eat → ate, see → saw, buy → bought, have → had, come → came. In questions and negatives use did + the base verb: Did you go? I didn't go (not “didn't went”).

examples.en: I went to the market and bought some fruit.
examples.ar: ذهبت إلى السوق واشتريت بعض الفاكهة.

dialogue.en: How was your weekend?
Great! I went to the old city with my family.
dialogue.ar: رائعة! ذهبت إلى المدينة القديمة مع عائلتي.

dialogue.en: What did you do there?
We saw the old market and I bought a scarf.
Did you eat there?
Yes, we had lunch in a small restaurant.
dialogue.ar: نعم، تناولنا الغداء في مطعم صغير.
